text:
oliver: copying the Python quickstart into an IPython notebook and hitting a snag. sample code:
```py
from redwood import AsyncClient
client = AsyncClient()
resp = client.chat.completions.create(model="gpt-4o", input="hi")
print(resp.output_text)
```
I run the cell and get: RuntimeError: asyncio.run() cannot be called from a running event loop.

priya: yeah that's a classic notebook thing — IPython already runs an event loop. The quickstart shows a sync-like call but our sync helper calls asyncio.run under the hood. For notebooks we should either: use `await` or show an explicit async cell example.

oliver: tried `await client.chat.completions.create(...)` in the cell, but `client` wasn't a context manager yet and I got `RuntimeError: Event loop is closed` on kernel restart. Repro steps attached above.

sam: can you paste the exact stacktrace? Quick tip: `from redwood import AsyncClient
client = AsyncClient()
await client.__aenter__()
# then await client.chat...
await client.__aexit__(None, None, None)` — that avoids asyncio.run. Alternately install `nest_asyncio` in the notebook.

oliver: stack: `File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/redwood/sdk.py", line 123, in create 
    return asyncio.run(self._create(...))` so looks like our public convenience API is still calling asyncio.run. That makes the quickstart copy-paste unsafe in notebooks.

mia: this is actually two separate DX problems: (1) the quickstart snippet suggests a sync usage without clarifying notebook caveats, (2) the sync wrapper behavior calling asyncio.run during import/first call can cause event-loop conflicts and also tear down background tasks incorrectly on kernel restart. I've reproduced with sample-app-quickstart and a tiny test notebook.

priya: agree — we should add a dedicated "Notebook" section in the Quickstart showing both async and sync-safe patterns. Also we should change the sync wrapper to avoid always using asyncio.run; instead prefer creating an internal background loop only when not already in a running loop or document it clearly.

sam: filing a GH issue now with repro + minimal notebook. Will link the issue in the thread. Also adding a small code example using `IPython.display` to show proper async usage.

docs-bot: created issue #1789: "Quickstart: AsyncClient and IPython/event-loop conflicts (notebook reproducible)" with the repro notebook attached.

oliver: awesome — thanks. tiny ask: can we also mention token refresh background task in the issue? I noticed if you use the sync convenience wrapper that starts the auth refresher, it sometimes tries to spawn tasks on a closed loop when the kernel restarts. Might be separate but worth tracking.

mia: noted in the issue. Proposed action items: 1) docs PR adding notebook patterns + callouts, 2) change sync wrapper to detect running loop and fallback to using an executor or raise a clear error, 3) add an integration test that runs our sample notebook in CI with papermill.

priya: sounds good. tagging @devex-squad to prioritize docs PR for next sprint.

oliver: thanks y'all! I'll follow the GH issue and test patches when available. :thumbsup:
